chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Mada'ini, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar ibn Musa al-Sabati, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man performing ghusl from janabah while his garment is near him, and some of the water with which he is washing splashes onto the garment. He said: "Yes, there is no harm in it."

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm or legal problem in it
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: he performs ghusl, a ritual washing

ai.seo_question: Does water splashing from ghusl al-janabah onto clothing make the garment problematic?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on ritual purity during ghusl from janabah. It states that if water from the ghusl reaches a nearby garment, there is no problem with it, indicating the absence of impurity or legal objection in such contact.
